correctness.rationale: The two endpoint-annihilation counterexamples are exact. For a two-eigenvalue quadratic the first local-curvature value is strictly between the endpoint eigenvalues when both initial endpoint components are nonzero. A seed equal to the reciprocal of one endpoint eigenvalue kills that eigenspace in the seed step, after which the running estimator can never recover the missing endpoint and the displayed nonoptimal constant stepsize follows. The separate summable-step construction is also valid: both scalar products remain positive, so the higher mode does not vanish relatively and the local curvature cannot tend to the smallest eigenvalue. The two repairs correctly add, respectively, endpoint persistence and enough cumulative step mass. The concrete instance with endpoint eigenvalues 1 and 2 was independently recomputed and gives the stated constants.
